thread:
carol.ng: Starting the scheduled BIOS+BMC rollout in eu-west-1 at 03:00UTC. About 150 nodes targeted, batch 3 (GPU racks). Rolling now, will post updates.
infra-bot: Alert: 12 nodes in eu-west-1 reported unexpected power-cycle during maintenance window (ids: gpu-ew1-0452,gpu-ew1-0453,gpu-ew1-0499,...). See /alerts/1769954321
carol.ng: Seeing some nodes come back but GPUs not present in lspci on a few. Example: gpu-ew1-0452 boots but no NVIDIA devices.
raj.patel: Can you paste ipmitool mc info and the kernel dmesg for one of the bad hosts? Might be BMC toggling secure-boot flag during fw apply.
carol.ng: ipmitool mc info output for gpu-ew1-0452:\n```
Device ID                 : 32
Device Revision           : 1
Firmware Revision         : 2.12
Manufacturer ID           : 42817
Product ID                : 328
Provides Device SDRs      : no
```
And dmesg snippet: \n```
[   12.345678] NVRM: loading NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  525.105.17  Thu Mar  2 11:22:13 UTC 2026
[   12.345700] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[   12.400000] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[   12.400010] nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_pci_probe
```
looks like driver didn't bind (PCI not enumerated properly).
maria_sre: Hmm, if secure boot was toggled off->on or on->off mid-boot that can change kernel module signing expectations. Any change logs from the fw-update controller for that batch?
carol.ng: Controller log shows: `bmc-update agent: toggling secure_boot = disabled -> enabled` for nodes in that batch. Not sure why. We only pushed BMC firmware 1.2.3 with vendor recommended flags.
raj.patel: That's the smoking gun. Some vendor firmware flips the BIOS secure boot variable when updating BMC. When secure boot becomes enabled, unsigned nvidia modules will be blocked and kernel refuses to load them -> GPUs invisible. Also OC VMs won't start.
dave_hw: Hardware ops: We've seen vendor image where the default secure boot keyring gets reset. Quick mitigation: set secure_boot to false in NVRAM before reboot, or re-enroll MOK if we want signed modules. For now I'd pause the rollout until we confirm behavior.
eva-ops: Adding context: this is only in eu-west-1 due to older BMC hardware (BMC rev 2.12). Other regions on newer revs don't flip the flag.
carol.ng: I can block remaining batches. Do we want a full rollback for affected nodes (reapply previous BMC fw) or a per-node manual secure-boot toggle? Which has less risk/cost?
raj.patel: Short term: manual secure-boot disable via ipmitool raw or vendor CLI and reboot to bring GPUs back. Longer term: pin to previous fw and open vendor PR. Manual steps (tested on gpu-ew1-0452):\n```
# check current variable
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** raw 0x0c 0x01
# vendor tool: set secure boot off
vendor-bmc-cli --host $BMC set-secure-boot --value off
reboot
```
Note: vendor-bmc-cli requires root on bastion.
maria_sre: Also add a guard in the rollout controller: detect secure-boot state diff post-update and auto-fail the node and alert instead of continuing.
infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-042 eu-west BMC fw causing secure-boot toggles. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INF-2026-042
dave_hw: I'm coordinating a small on-call team to walk through manual remediation. ETA 25m for first batch of 6 nodes. Requesting no more rollouts in eu-west until this is cleared.
eva-ops: Tags: @oncall @eng-platform @eng-runtime. Cost note: if we keep these nodes down longer, we'll need to shift jobs to another region; scheduling and egress costs may spike.
carol.ng: Paused rollout. I've placed the remaining eu-west batches on hold in the controller UI.
raj.patel: I'll push a quick fix to the rollout service to detect vendor fw versions >=2.12 and block automatic secure-boot changes (feature-flagged). PR coming in 10m.
maria_sre: Creating a post-incident checklist: rollback steps + communicate to customers of Dedicated capacity in eu-west for degraded throughput. Warn support.
carol.ng: Remediation update: manually toggled secure-boot -> off on gpu-ew1-0452 and gpu-ew1-0453, rebooted, `lspci | grep -i nvidia` now shows devices. Performing health checks on CUDA tests.
infra-bot: Update: 6/12 impacted nodes remediated, 6 still pending.
dave_hw: For the remaining nodes we may need physical console access for ones with intermittent BMC network. Looping in on-site techs.
eva-ops: Communication plan ready. Draft sent to SRE-SUPPORT for customer-facing note. Will wait until 80% remediation.
raj.patel: After we finish manual fixes, we should re-run a lab case with the fw image to reproduce secure-boot flip and document exact steps to vendor.
maria_sre: Also add an automated eval in CI: fw-update job runs on a copy of a test-node and checks NVRAM secure_boot variable before/after. Fail rollouts on unexpected flips.
carol.ng: Thanks everyone. I’ll keep thread updates here and attach logs to INF-2026-042. If anyone sees other regions showing similar symptoms, ping immediately. :white_check_mark:
